Cancer Center at Illinois earns prestigious National Cancer Institute designation
The first designation of its kind in nearly 40 years recognizes the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign’s transformative research in cancer diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Bioengineering faculty and researchers contribute significant efforts within the Cancer Center, led by bioengineering professor and Phillip and Ann Sharp Director Rohit Bhargava.

Hijacking a Handshake: Illinois Bioengineering Professor Jenny Amos Demonstrates Neural Implant Vulnerabilities on Capitol Hill
Bioengineering News
October 12, 2026
Laura Hahn Teaching Professor Jenny Amos brought a live, interactive neurotechnology demonstration to Capitol Hill for the Coalition for National Science Foundation (CNSF) Congressional Showcase to raise awareness of neural implant vulnerabilities. She was selected to present by the American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering (AIMBE), which is a non-profit organization that focuses on advocacy, public engagement, and programs on elevating medical and biological engineering.

Engineering the Bioeconomy
Bioengineering News
September 8, 2026
The bioeconomy is an economic model that converts renewable biological resources into life essentials. While the idea is simple — turning atmospheric carbon into a microbe-friendly food source and recovering leftover nutrients to repeat the cycle indefinitely — the execution is much more challenging. But for Illinois faculty, like bioengineering professor Ting Lu, the enormous benefits are worth the stakes: these minimal-resource technologies aim to bolster energy security and supply chain resilience, promote resource circularity, and address global challenges like climate change and food insecurity. “Biotechnology gives us an ability to manufacture in a different way,” said Lu. “We’re harnessing a living factory — a factory of programmable living organisms that takes up raw materials, processes them, and translates them into something valuable.

Genetic Base Editing Treats Huntingtonâs Disease in Mice
Bioengineering News
August 3, 2026
A gene editing tool designed to precisely rewrite the gene that causes Huntington’s disease reduced toxic protein fragments and symptoms associated with the disease in mice, researchers at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign report. While other gene-based treatments have focused on turning the gene off, the Illinois team took a different approach. The researchers designed a base-editing tool to alter a specific point of the huntingtin gene so the cell’s machinery would skip over a small section prone to generating toxic fragments, while preserving enough protein to support its normal functions. Led by Pablo Perez-Pinera and Thomas Gaj, professors of bioengineering at the U. of I., the researchers published their findings in the journal Nature Biomedical Engineering.

Illinois-Led Team Selected for DOE Genesis Mission Award
Bioengineering News
July 24, 2026
A multidisciplinary team led by U. of I. chemical and biomolecular engineering professor Huimin Zhao has received a Phase I award through the U.S. Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission to develop the world’s first foundation models specifically designed for metabolic engineering. “Biological design presents an enormous challenge because of the complexity of genes, enzymes, metabolic pathways and environmental interactions,” Zhao said. “Our goal is to create artificial intelligence foundation models that can learn from diverse biological data and help scientists predict and design new biological functions much more efficiently than is possible today.”
Read more
Bioengineering Professor Yang Liu Advances Immunofluorescence
Bioengineering News
July 20, 2026
Bioengineering professor Yang Liu’s team, including first author Phuong “Hong” Nguyen, has developed a novel approach to immunofluorescence that is easier, faster, and more accessible. The discovery, called Universal Multiplexed Immunofluorescence (umIF), is outlined in a paper published in Small Methods. "Our goal was not simply to create another multiplexed [immunofluorescence] protocol," said Liu, "but to make spatial protein profiling more practical for real clinical specimens and large-scale tissue mapping studies.”

Capstone
The bioengineering capstone experience provides undergraduate and professional masters students the opportunity to design solutions to projects provided by academia, industry and clinical settings. Utilizing principles of design, engineering analysis and functional operation of engineering systems, students tackle real-world challenges and data sets in partnership with capstone project sponsors.

Everitt Lab
At 124,000 square feet of state of the art laboratories, classrooms and community spaces, Everitt Lab is the central hub for all things bioengineering. Renovated in 2018, the building also houses state of the art medical training facilities such as Carle Illinois' JUMP Simulation Center.
